nodes.description: Melanoma arising on glabrous acral skin (palms, soles, digits, and nail beds), originating as an irregularly pigmented lentiginous macule independent of UV radiation exposure and frequently presenting at an advanced stage.

evidence.reference_title: Somatic activation of KIT in distinct subtypes of melanoma.
evidence.snippet: mutations and/or copy number increases of KIT in 39% of mucosal, 36% of acral, and 28% of melanomas on chronically sun-damaged skin, but not in any (0%) melanomas on skin without chronic sun damage

evidence.reference_title: Acral Lentiginous Melanoma.
evidence.snippet: Unlike other CMM, UV-radiation is not thought to play a significant part in the development of ALM. It is most commonly on the lower extremities and is often advanced at the time of presentation leading to a high level of morbidity and mortality.

nodes.description: PI3K-AKT and anti-apoptotic signaling downstream of constitutively active KIT suppresses intrinsic apoptotic execution in malignant melanocytes, conferring oncogene dependence reversible upon KIT kinase inhibition.

evidence.reference_title: Imatinib targeting of KIT-mutant oncoprotein in melanoma.
evidence.snippet: In vitro analyses revealed major sensitivity to KIT kinase inhibition by imatinib, with potent induction of melanoma cell apoptosis.

nodes.description: Cutaneous melanoma harboring somatic KIT mutations, occurring predominantly on chronically sun-damaged skin (head, neck, and distal extremities) and rarely (<5%) on intermittently sun-exposed trunk skin.

evidence.reference_title: KIT-Mutant Melanoma: Understanding the Pathway to Personalized Therapy.
evidence.snippet: Population-level studies estimate that approximately 11–23% of acral melanomas, 15–21% of mucosal melanomas, and up to 27% of CSD melanomas harbor KIT mutations, whereas the prevalence in non-CSD cutaneous melanoma is generally less than 5%

nodes.description: Multitarget kinase inhibitor with activity against KIT, ABL, and SRC family kinases. Phase II ECOG-ACRIN E2607 data showed modest, short-lived responses (18.2% PR in stage II KIT+ cohort; median PFS 2.1 months) and substantial toxicity, so imatinib remains preferred over dasatinib.

evidence.reference_title: A phase 2 trial of dasatinib in patients with locally advanced or stage IV mucosal, acral, or vulvovaginal melanoma: A trial of the ECOG-ACRIN Cancer Research Group (E2607).
evidence.snippet: it is recommended that imatinib remain the KIT tyrosine kinase inhibitor of choice for unresectable KIT+ melanoma

nodes.description: First-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting KIT, ABL, and PDGFR and the preferred front-line KIT TKI for unresectable or metastatic melanoma harboring activating exon 11 (L576P, pooled ORR 52%) or exon 13 (K642E, pooled ORR 42%) KIT mutations, whereas amplification-only disease lacks objective response.

evidence.reference_title: Imatinib for melanomas harboring mutationally activated or amplified KIT arising on mucosal, acral, and chronically sun-damaged skin.
evidence.snippet: Best overall response rate (BORR) was 29% (21% excluding nonconfirmed responses) with a two-stage 95% CI of 13% to 51%.

evidence.reference_title: KIT as a therapeutic target in metastatic melanoma.
evidence.snippet: The overall durable response rate was 16%

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and genomic correlates of imatinib response in melanomas with KIT alterations.
evidence.snippet: In the pooled analysis (N = 130), alterations in exons 11/13 had the highest response rates (38% and 33%); L576P (N = 23) and K642E (N = 12) mutations had ORR of 52% and 42%, respectively.

evidence.reference_title: c-Kit inhibitors for unresectable or metastatic mucosal, acral or chronically sun-damaged melanoma: a systematic review and one-arm meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: The pooled ORR for all inhibitors was 15%

nodes.description: KIT-mutant melanoma cells exhibit JAK-STAT pathway activation downstream of constitutive KIT kinase activity, supporting proliferative and pro-survival transcriptional programs alongside MAPK and PI3K-AKT cascades.

evidence.reference_title: Imatinib targeting of KIT-mutant oncoprotein in melanoma.
evidence.snippet: Exposure to drug affected the mitogen-activated protein kinase, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/AKT, JAK-STAT, and antiapoptotic pathways.

evidence.reference_title: Somatic activation of KIT in distinct subtypes of melanoma.
evidence.snippet: Seventy-nine percent of tumors with mutations and 53% of tumors with multiple copies of KIT demonstrated increased KIT protein levels.

meta.presence: Increased KIT protein expression and receptor phosphorylation in KIT-mutated and KIT-amplified melanomas

readouts.interpretation: Reflects constitutive KIT receptor phosphorylation and elevated protein expression in tumor tissue.

meta.term_label: Mast/Stem Cell Growth Factor Receptor Kit

meta.association: Somatic copy-number gain at 4q12 with or without concurrent point mutation

evidence.reference_title: Imatinib for melanomas harboring mutationally activated or amplified KIT arising on mucosal, acral, and chronically sun-damaged skin.
evidence.snippet: BORR was significantly greater than the hypothesized null of 5% and statistically significantly different by mutation status (7 of 13 or 54% KIT mutated v 0% KIT amplified only).

evidence.snippet: Exon 11 is the most frequently affected, accounting for approximately 50–60% of cases, and includes the L576P mutation, which alone represents about 30% of all reported KIT mutations.

evidence.reference_title: KIT as a therapeutic target in metastatic melanoma.
evidence.snippet: all 6 responses occurred in tumors with L576P or K642E mutations, the most common mutations in melanoma

meta.association: Recurrent kinase domain I somatic driver (~10-15% of KIT-mutant melanomas)

evidence.reference_title: KIT-Mutant Melanoma: Understanding the Pathway to Personalized Therapy.
evidence.snippet: Exon 13, part of the kinase domain I, harbors the K642E mutation, observed in 10 to 15% of KIT-mutant melanoma cases

evidence.reference_title: Pathological activation of KIT in metastatic tumors of acral and mucosal melanomas.
evidence.snippet: Sequence analysis revealed K642E and D820Y mutations in two metastases.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and genomic correlates of imatinib response in melanomas with KIT alterations.
evidence.snippet: In the pooled analysis (N = 130), alterations in exons 11/13 had the highest response rates (38% and 33%); L576P (N = 23) and K642E (N = 12) mutations had ORR of 52% and 42%, respectively.

meta.association: Activation-loop somatic driver (~5-10% of KIT-mutant melanomas)

evidence.reference_title: Pathological activation of KIT in metastatic tumors of acral and mucosal melanomas.

evidence.reference_title: KIT-Mutant Melanoma: Understanding the Pathway to Personalized Therapy.
evidence.snippet: Mutations that occur in exon 17 include the D820Y mutation and others that comprise roughly 5–10% of the mutational burden.

nodes.description: Somatic KIT mutations, most commonly clustering in exon 11 (juxtamembrane autoinhibitory domain, e.g., L576P), exon 13 (kinase domain I, e.g., K642E), and exon 17 (activation loop, e.g., D820Y), induce ligand-independent receptor dimerization, loss of autoinhibition, and constitutive KIT phosphorylation independent of stem cell factor (SCF) binding, and are usually mutually exclusive with BRAF and NRAS driver mutations.

biological_processes: cell surface receptor protein tyrosine kinase signaling pathway

evidence.reference_title: c-KIT Small Molecule Inhibitors as a Therapeutic Strategy for Melanoma: Clinical Insights, SAR, and Future Directions.
evidence.snippet: Mutation of c-KIT has been observed in acral, mucosal, and chronically sun-damaged melanoma subtypes marking it as a key therapeutic target for melanoma.

evidence.reference_title: Somatic activation of KIT in distinct subtypes of melanoma.
evidence.snippet: mutations and/or copy number increases of KIT in 39% of mucosal, 36% of acral, and 28% of melanomas on chronically sun-damaged skin, but not in any (0%) melanomas on skin without chronic sun damage

evidence.reference_title: KIT-Mutant Melanoma: Understanding the Pathway to Personalized Therapy.
evidence.snippet: Notably, KIT mutations are usually mutually exclusive of BRAF and NRAS mutations, which are the most common oncogenic drivers in cutaneous melanoma

evidence.reference_title: Therapeutic implications of KIT in melanoma.
evidence.snippet: Activating mutations in KIT have been discovered in a significant proportion of melanomas arising from acral, mucosal, and chronically sun-damaged sites and represent an important melanoma genetic subset.

evidence.reference_title: Pathological activation of KIT in metastatic tumors of acral and mucosal melanomas.
evidence.snippet: Western blot analysis showed phosphorylation of the KIT receptor in 8 (62%) of 13 cryopreserved samples, indicating the frequent pathological activation of the receptor in vivo.

molecular_functions: transmembrane receptor protein tyrosine kinase activity

nodes.description: Melanoma arising in chronically sun-damaged skin (especially head and neck regions), where up to ~27-28% of tumors harbor KIT mutations or copy-number increases.

evidence.reference_title: Somatic activation of KIT in distinct subtypes of melanoma.
evidence.snippet: mutations and/or copy number increases of KIT in 39% of mucosal, 36% of acral, and 28% of melanomas on chronically sun-damaged skin, but not in any (0%) melanomas on skin without chronic sun damage

nodes.description: Activated KIT recruits adapter proteins (GRB2/SOS) that engage RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK signaling, driving melanocyte proliferation through ERK-mediated cell-cycle transcriptional programs.

evidence.reference_title: Imatinib targeting of KIT-mutant oncoprotein in melanoma.
evidence.snippet: Exposure to drug affected the mitogen-activated protein kinase, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/AKT, JAK-STAT, and antiapoptotic pathways.

nodes.description: Malignant melanocytic neoplasm driven by somatic activating KIT alterations across mucosal, acral, or chronically sun-damaged primary sites.

evidence.reference_title: Somatic activation of KIT in distinct subtypes of melanoma.
evidence.snippet: KIT is an important oncogene in melanoma.

nodes.description: Second-generation KIT-selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor demonstrating an ORR of 26.2% (enriched in exon 11/L576P) in the global phase II TEAM trial, 19% 12-week ORR in the phase II NICAM trial for KIT-mutated mucosal and acral melanoma, and objective responses (16% ORR, 52.6% disease control rate) in patients with prior imatinib exposure.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of nilotinib in patients with KIT-mutated metastatic or inoperable melanoma: final results from the global, single-arm, phase II TEAM trial.
evidence.snippet: ORR was 26.2% (n = 11/42; 95% CI, 13.9%-42.0%), sufficient to reject the null hypothesis (ORR ≤10%). All observed responses were partial responses (PRs; median response duration, 7.1 months).

evidence.reference_title: Nilotinib in KIT-driven advanced melanoma: Results from the phase II single-arm NICAM trial.
evidence.snippet: KIT mutations are identified in 39/219 screened patients (18%); of 29/39 treated, 26 are evaluable for primary analysis. Six patients were alive and progression free at 6 months (local radiology review, 25%); 5/26 (19%) had objective response at 12 weeks; median OS was 7.7 months; ddPCR assay correctly identifies KIT alterations in circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in 16/17 patients.

evidence.reference_title: KIT-Mutant Melanoma: Understanding the Pathway to Personalized Therapy.
evidence.snippet: Meanwhile, the study by Carvajal et al. in patients with prior imatinib exposure found an ORR of 16% at 12 weeks and DCR of 52.6%

evidence.reference_title: c-Kit inhibitors for unresectable or metastatic mucosal, acral or chronically sun-damaged melanoma: a systematic review and one-arm meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: Subgroup analysis revealed the highest ORR (20%; 95% CI: 14-26%) for nilotinib.

nodes.description: KIT activates PI3K through recruitment and phosphorylation of p85 adapter subunits; subsequent AKT and mTOR activation promotes melanoma cell survival and inhibits pro-apoptotic effectors.

evidence.reference_title: Imatinib targeting of KIT-mutant oncoprotein in melanoma.
evidence.snippet: Exposure to drug affected the mitogen-activated protein kinase, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/AKT, JAK-STAT, and antiapoptotic pathways.

nodes.description: Broad-spectrum type II switch-control KIT/PDGFRA tyrosine kinase inhibitor evaluated in KIT-altered metastatic melanoma, achieving a 23% confirmed objective response rate and 7.3-month median progression-free survival overall in phase I expansion testing, with higher activity in KIT-inhibitor-naive patients (29% ORR, 10.2-month mPFS) than in previously TKI-treated patients (11% ORR, 2.9-month mPFS).

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of ripretinib in patients with KIT-altered metastatic melanoma.
evidence.snippet: Confirmed objective response rate (ORR) was 23%

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of ripretinib in patients with KIT-altered metastatic melanoma.
evidence.snippet: Median progression-free survival (mPFS) was 7.3 months (95% CI 1.9-13.6 months).

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of ripretinib in patients with KIT-altered metastatic melanoma.
evidence.snippet: Patients without prior KIT inhibitor therapy had a higher ORR and longer mPFS (n = 17, ORR 29%, mPFS 10.2 months) than those who had received prior KIT inhibitor treatment (n = 9, ORR 11%, mPFS 2.9 months).

nodes.description: Constitutive KIT signaling through MAPK, PI3K-AKT, and JAK-STAT pathways drives sustained growth-factor-independent melanocyte proliferation across acral, mucosal, and chronically sun-damaged sites, initiating invasive melanoma growth.

evidence.reference_title: Imatinib targeting of KIT-mutant oncoprotein in melanoma.
evidence.snippet: Imatinib dramatically decreased proliferation and was cytotoxic to a KIT mutated and amplified cell culture.
